evidence.quote: SWMU 29 East Landfarm This unit is a RCRA-regulated unit which is part of the East Hill SWMA. It was closed in 1988 and entered post-closure care in 1992. It is roughly kidney shaped and covers approximately 3.7 acres, including a 0.3-acre stormwater basin. In 2015, the Permittee requested that groundwater monitoring and care for the East Landfarm be managed through the RCRA Corrective Action program and the EPA HSWA Permit. Because the East Landfarm was built on top of AOC 82 and adjacent to SWMU Nos. 1 – 4, SWMU No. 60, and AOC No. 72, some contamination from these East Hill units is intermingled, and thus, the East Hill units are being addressed together with the other units in the East Hill SWMA. Upon issuance of this Permit, the alternative requirements, outlined in the Permittee’s 2020 East Landfarm Long-Term Care Plan, will apply to the East Landfarm. These requirements, similar to those previously specified in MDEQ’s 2006 Permit, consist of institutional controls, inspections, monitoring, maintenance, run-on and run-off controls, security systems, and groundwater monitoring conducted in accordance with the latest approved versions of the East Hill Groundwater Monitoring Plan and the QAPP for the Corrective Action Program.

MNA-plan submission separately uses 60 days from effectiveness and implementation follows written approval. question: For facility-089, join the pinned Chevron Pascagoula sources to the official FRS/program rows: explain why acceptance of Comment 28 does not imply acceptance of Comment 29 or release of ongoing work.
answer: EPA accepted deletion of the eight-acre former Catalyst Disposal Area sentence from SWMU 10/Lagoon 3’s description in Comment 28. The adjacent requested replacement narrative in Comment 29 is marked Permit Unchanged. The final permit retains agency completion and financial-assurance release gates. A corrected site-description sentence does not approve every proffered historical/NFA characterization or establish present unrestricted use, removal of remaining conditions or closure of the entire corrective-action schedule.

evidence.quote: 28 Comment Comment Number 28 requests that the EPA revise the existing text of the SWMU description for SWMU 10 (Lagoon No. 3) located in Table A-1 of Appendix A of the Permit. The Comment provides the following statement as justification for the request: “The designation of ‘Catalyst Disposal Area’ within Lagoon No. 3 does not seem valid. Reviews of historical documents and refinery personnel do not validate this location and/or description.” The description for SWMU 10 in Table A-1 of Appendix A has been changed. EPA Response The description for SWMU 10 in Table A-1 of Appendix A has been changed by deleting the following text: “The shallow area on the west side of Lagoon No. 3 includes the 8-acre former Catalyst Disposal Area.” 29 Comment Comment Number 29 requests that the EPA revise and replace the existing text for the SWMU description for SWMU 10 (Lagoon No. 3) located in Table A-1 of Appendix A of the Permit. The Comment provides the following statement as justification for the request: “In the event that EPA needs clarification of past disposal practices involving Lagoon No. 3, replace existing text with the following: As a result of the ecological risk assessment, a habitat removal project was conducted during 2008-2009 to remove the site attractive nuisance designation, imposed by EPA. As documented in the Construction Completion Report (September 2009) which summarized habitat removal activities, sediments in the area on the west side of the lagoon were dewatered, excavated, solidified with Portland cement slurry and placed in lifts into the Consolidation Cell located along the southwestern border of the lagoon. The cell was capped, completely isolating and immobilizing sediments. The pond was then returned to industrial use as part of the NPDES stormwater retention system. evidence.quote: II.L. COMPLETION OF CORRECTIVE ACTION (40 CFR § 264.101) II.L.1. The Corrective Action shall be considered complete when the Regional Administrator determines that: (a) compliance with the media cleanup standards and the CAOs in Appendix D has been achieved; and (b) all actions required to control the source(s) of contamination have been satisfied. II.L.2. Corrective Action shall be considered complete with or without controls in place where the Permittee has satisfied all obligations under RCRA Sections 3004(u) and (v). II.L.3. Upon completion of the Corrective Action for the entire Facility, or a portion of the Facility, or any off-site contamination, the Permittee may submit to the Regional Administrator, by certified mail, a request for termination of the Corrective Action Schedule of Compliance according to the procedures for Class 3 modifications in 40 CFR § 270.42. The request shall include a certification that the Corrective Measures have been completed in accordance with the requirements set forth by the Regional Administrator. II.L.4. When, upon receipt of the certification, and in consideration of public comments and any other relevant information, the Regional Administrator determines that the Corrective Measures have been completed in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Permit and the requirements for completion, the Regional Administrator will: a) terminate the HSWA Permit; or b) modify the Permit to terminate the Corrective Action Schedule of Compliance for SWMUs and AOCs that require no further action at this time. Upon termination of the Permit, or modification of the Permit for completion of Corrective Action at the entire Facility, the EPA will release the Permittee from the financial assurance requirements of this Permit. II.M. CORRECTIVE
